faq.q: What is the origin of Thiziri?
faq.a: Thiziri is associated with Amazigh. Thiziri is Amazigh (Berber), meaning 'moonlight'.
No — the underlying form is Amazigh, not Arabic.
Thiziri can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Amazigh-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Thiziri should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Thiziri is an Amazigh word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Thiziri mean in Persian?

faq.q: What are the variants of Thiziri?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Thiziri, thiziri. Script forms are ثيزيري, ثِيزِيرِي, ثیزیری, थिज़ीरी.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
